goal: stress R2 grid/scroll/images at 30/100/300 cards and 1000 synthetic nodes

host.warp_caveat: Microsoft Basic Render Driver (WARP) over D3D12: software rasterizer, CPU/commit memory. Timings are not representative of a hardware GPU; readback/map and WARP pass costs dominate the offscreen frame.

method.compile: cl /nologo /O2 /W3 /std:c17 /TC /D_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS /DWN_STATIC <runtime_r2.c wn_core.c wn_common.c> + wgpu_native.dll.lib, same sources/flags as src/runtime/c-r2/build.ps1 (unmodified)
method.layout: runtime --report runs 100 layout_page() iterations per size; this report takes the median across process runs of layout_ms_best and layout_ms_avg. Report layout excludes display-list/geometry build.
method.render: one cold process per run: --render W H out.png. wall_ms is measured around Popen (includes process + wgpu/WARP init). frame_ms is the runtime's printed frame line: pass + readback + png, measured after layout, build_geometry and vertex upload (the runtime label says 'build+upload' but the timer starts after them). layout_ms is printed separately and excludes geometry build.
method.wheel: --render W H out.png --wheel X Y DY. Offset/max are parsed from the runtime's wheel:/scroll: lines; the accent band's pixel Y in the PNG is the independent position check (poster rule band maps to card.y+166..173 after object-fit:cover).
method.image_cache: --states prefix --size 1280x800 renders 4 frames in one process: the first is cold (WIC decode + upload), frames 2-4 reuse the path-keyed cache. decode_overhead = cold - warm frame.
method.memory: GetProcessMemoryInfo sampled every ~4 ms while the process runs; peak WorkingSetSize / PeakPagefileUsage. WARP dominates commit.
timing_note: The printed frame label is misleading: build_geometry() and gpu_upload_geometry() run before the frame timer starts, so frame_ms = gpu pass + readback(map) + png.
Wheel events that change the offset trigger an extra full layout inside wn_core_wheel(); it is not included in the printed layout_ms or frame_ms.
Image decode happens inside gpu_draw(), so it is inside the runtime's frame/gpu timing.
Offscreen readback (map) + PNG encode are measured by the runtime but are not representative of a windowed present.
method.png_verification: Pillow: exact accent-colour band positions (poster rule band), no accent outside the grid rect, PNG dimensions, synthetic cell colours present.

bottlenecks.evidence: same-template offscreen frame 30 cards=190.0 ms, 300 cards=193.0 ms (x1.02); solid vertices 300 -> 1920, while glyph/image vertices stay at 4170 / 90
bottlenecks.note: Viewport culling bounds text/image draws; solid card rectangles still grow with the catalogue (6 vertices per card).

bottlenecks.evidence: layout median avg: 300 cards (2718 nodes)=0.300 ms, 1000 synthetic nodes=0.067 ms at 1280x800 (layout ≈ 0.16% of the 300-card offscreen frame)
bottlenecks.note: Layout is sub-millisecond; offscreen pass/readback/PNG dominate.

bottlenecks.evidence: cards-300 1280x800 frame components: gpu=17.9%, readback(map)=60.5%, png=19.8% (frame 193.0 ms, wall 477.6 ms)
bottlenecks.recommendation: Do not use the offscreen frame as a GPU benchmark. Report pass, readback and PNG separately (done) and measure windowed present for real frame cost.

bottlenecks.evidence: cards-300 cold frame=184.1 ms vs warm frame=91.7 ms (+92.5 ms on the first frame). 300 image nodes reuse 30 unique posters and only the viewport-visible unique files decode.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Keep the path-keyed cache, but add LRU/refcount eviction by bytes and decode to display size; a 180x240 RGBA texture is ~169 KiB.

bottlenecks.evidence: cards-300 1280x800 peak working set=77.9 MB, peak pagefile=361.6 MB; WARP device commit dominates and barely moves between 30 and 300 cards.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Track image-cache bytes separately from WARP commit; the cache is the part that grows with a real 1000-poster library.

bottlenecks.evidence: runtime vertices grow linearly with cards (cards-030=300, cards-100=720, cards-300=1920 at 1280x800; +6 vertices/card), while image_vertices stay at 90 and glyph_vertices at ~4.2k. Every card background is emitted even when far below the scroll clip.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Cull solid rects by the scroll viewport (or window rows) in wn_core_build_display_list, not just image/glyph batches.

bottlenecks.evidence: When a wheel delta changes the offset, wn_core_wheel() calls layout_page() for the whole document; render_offscreen() also lays out before applying the wheel, so that wheel frame performs two full layouts. At 300 cards layout is 0.300 ms each; the second one is outside both printed layout_ms and frame_ms.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Make scroll offset-only (translate rects / adjust scissor) and count it in frame timing. Reserve relayout for resize.

bottlenecks.evidence: All cards are laid out and all solid geometry is built each frame; only image/glyph draws are clipped. 300 cards = 2718 nodes; a 1000-card A1 library would be ~9000 nodes and ~6000 solid vertices.
bottlenecks.recommendation: For 500-1000+ items, virtualize rows: keep visible + overscan cards and recycle nodes. This bounds layout, solid geometry and memory.

bottlenecks.evidence: Each image batch owns one bind group and one draw; batches merge only for consecutive identical src+clip. With cycled posters the visible set is ~15 images at 1280x800; a unique-image grid approaches one draw per visible image.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Atlas/array textures + instanced quads or grouped multi-draw.

bottlenecks.evidence: Microsoft Basic Render Driver (WARP) over D3D12: software rasterizer, CPU/commit memory. Timings are not representative of a hardware GPU; readback/map and WARP pass costs dominate the offscreen frame.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Treat these numbers as a CPU/WARP lower bound and a regression baseline, not as hardware-GPU performance.

recommendations: Scroll: offset-only update (no full relayout) and include it in frame timing.
Cull solid card rects by viewport/row window; images/glyphs are already clipped.
Virtualize the grid for 500+ cards; measure layout + geometry per frame.
Image cache: LRU by bytes, decode to display size, atlas/array + instancing.
Expose geometry-build time, batch count and draw count in --render/--report.
Keep the current viewport culling: image_vertices stayed at 90 (1280x800) for 30 and 300 cards.
Add a warm-render/--frames N offscreen mode so cache and frame costs can be measured without --states or a window.
Re-run this suite on a hardware GPU; WARP readback/PNG obscures GPU cost.
